title: Wayanad Coffee Roasters — cold-store expansion NPV and IRR
narrative:
Wayanad Coffee Roasters is evaluating a cold-store expansion that would cut spoilage on aged green beans and support a new institutional contract. The project requires an immediate capital outlay and is expected to generate constant annual after-tax operating cash flows for five years, with an after-tax salvage value at the end of year 5 (Exhibit 1).

The company's hurdle rate for projects of this risk class is 10%. Present-value factors are supplied in Exhibit 2 so that all candidates use the same discounting basis. Ignore inflation and assume cash flows arise at each year-end.

tasks.prompt: Calculate the project's NPV at the 10% hurdle rate.
tasks.hint: Whole dollars, no commas. Use Exhibit 2 factors.

tasks.prompt: Calculate the project's accounting / simple payback period in years (ignore salvage and discounting).
Calculate the project's profitability index at 10% (PV of inflows / initial outlay).

tasks.hint: Whole dollars. Sign: enter as a positive number if NPV is positive.

tasks.prompt: Using linear interpolation between 12% and 14%, complete the IRR statement.

fields.label: and the interpolated IRR is closest to

tasks.prompt: Which conclusions follow from the analysis? Select all that apply.

options: At the 10% hurdle rate the project creates shareholder value.
A profitability index above 1.0 is consistent with a positive NPV.
Payback alone is sufficient to accept the project under shareholder-value criteria.
If the hurdle rate rose to 14%, NPV would turn negative and the project would be rejected.

tasks.explanation: Positive NPV at 10%, IRR ~ 13.2% > 10%, and PI > 1 are aligned accept signals. Payback ignores time value and cash flows beyond recovery, so it is not sufficient alone. At 14% NPV is negative, so the project fails that hurdle.

tasks.prompt: Match each capital-budgeting metric to the description that best fits it.

zones.abs: Absolute dollar value added to wealth
zones.rate: Break-even discount rate on the project's cash flows
zones.time: Time to recover the initial outlay from undiscounted CFs

tasks.explanation: NPV measures wealth increase in dollars; IRR is the rate that drives NPV to zero; payback counts recovery time; PI scales PV inflows to outlay for ranking under rationing.
